newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary govt security yields seen falling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary govt security yields seen falling.

text.p: Yields on Hungarian state securities on the secondary market were seen continuing do decline this week, dealers said on Monday.

Dealers said that on the secondary market yields on government bonds dropped by some 0.1 percentage points last week, while discount Treasury bill yields followed the trend at last year's auctions and fell by as much as 0.4 points.
One-year yields are between 22.25 and 22.35 percent, halk-year yields between 22.2 and 22.3 percents and one- and three-month yields around 22.1 percent. @

One dealer said that even the National Bank of Hungary regarded the fall of yields too quick last week, and intervened before the 12-month T-bill auction, selling from its own stock of papers, but the 12-month yield dropped below 22.5 percent.
Dealers said expectations of a decline in inflation and yields were strengthened last week, after the October CPI figure was published, showing year-on-year inflation at 21 percent. @

Dealers said T-bill yields were likely to drop further by 0.15 to 0.2 percentage points this week, while government bonds were expected to fall by 0.1 to 0.2 points, however opinions concerning the longer term outlooks of the market were mixed.
"There are many who say that the decline should stop between 21.5 and 22 percent," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities.
"But there are others who do not think it impossible that the yields will be around 20 percent by the end of the year," he added.
